templates.deleteMetaLocallyAria: Delete template from Meta and locally

templates.dialogNewDesc: Build a template and submit it to Meta for approval. Once approved, you can use it in broadcasts and the inbox.

templates.toastSubmitNewSuccess: Submitted to Meta — typical review time is 24 hours. Status updates automatically.

whatsapp.notRegistered: Not registered — Meta will not deliver events

calendly.desc: Connect Calendly so the CRM learns about every booked slot: the "Calendly booking" automation trigger finds the customer by phone, fills the fields, moves the card and notifies whoever you want. Calendly notifies the CRM instantly (webhook).
calendly.tokenVazio: Paste the token generated in Calendly
calendly.tokenDica: Calendly → Integrations → API & Webhooks → Personal access tokens → Generate new token. Use the account that administers the organization (to see everyone's events). The token is stored encrypted and never shown again.
calendly.planoDica: Webhooks require a paid Calendly plan (Standard or higher).
calendly.conectadoSemWebhook: Token accepted, but the webhook could not be subscribed. See the reason below and try Resubscribe.
calendly.webhookDesativado: Webhook DISABLED by Calendly (24h of failed deliveries) — resubscribe.
calendly.webhookAusente: No webhook subscribed — no bookings arrive until you resubscribe.
calendly.confirmarDesconectar: Disconnect Calendly? The webhook is removed and bookings stop arriving. The event history stays.
calendly.perguntaHint: You usually don't need this: the CRM finds the phone on its own, from the SMS reminder or from the form answer that looks like a phone (IDs and tax numbers are excluded). Fill it in only if your form has more than one phone-like question and the CRM picks the wrong one — then write part of the right question's label (e.g. WhatsApp). Each log row shows where the phone came from.
calendly.urlHint: This is the URL registered in Calendly. For reference only — the CRM subscribes it.
calendly.urlInalcancavel: The CRM's public URL (NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL) is not reachable from outside — the webhook cannot be subscribed from this environment.

tldv.resumo: {total} meeting(s) imported · {prontas} with transcript · {pendentes} waiting for tl;dv
tldv.confirmarDesconectar: Disconnect tl;dv? Meetings already imported stay on the clients' profiles; syncing stops.
tldv.semCliente: {n} meeting(s) without a client: link them below so they show up on the profile.
tldv.webhookAjuda: In tl;dv, under Settings → Webhooks, paste this URL and enable the MeetingReady and TranscriptReady events. Without it the meeting arrives on the next scheduler cycle (about 15 minutes, plus the time the other routes in the loop take).

channels.title: Connections
channels.description: Every WhatsApp number this workspace answers from — official Meta API numbers and QR-Code numbers, side by side.
channels.chooseInstagramDesc: Receives and answers Direct messages of a professional Instagram account. Only the person can start the conversation, and there are 24 hours to reply.
channels.instagramStepDescription: Register the Meta app once, then connect each professional account with Instagram login. You can also paste a token generated in the Meta dashboard.
channels.instagramAccessTokenHint: Generated in the Meta dashboard with the "Generate token" button. Valid for 60 days; the CRM warns when it is about to expire.
channels.instagramAppSecretHint: It is the key from the Instagram product tab, not the app's main secret key. It is what signs the messages Meta sends here.
channels.instagramHumanAgentHint: Turn on only after Meta approves the "Human Agent" feature for your app. Without the approval, replying after 24 hours is refused.
channels.instagramHelpToken_1: developers.facebook.com → your app → Instagram → API setup with Instagram login.
channels.instagramHelpToken_2: Under "Generate access tokens", add the professional Instagram account and click "Generate token".
channels.instagramHelpToken_3: On the same account, turn on the "Webhook subscription" switch — without it no message arrives.
channels.instagramHelpSecret: Where the Instagram App ID and App Secret are
channels.instagramHelpSecret_1: On that screen, in the product configuration block: the "Instagram App ID" and "Instagram App Secret" fields.
channels.instagramHelpSecret_2: Not the "App secret" under App settings → Basic: that one does not sign Instagram messages.
channels.instagramHelpWebhook_after: After connecting, the CRM shows the URL and the Verify Token for you to paste into the Meta dashboard. You can see them again anytime with the connection's "Webhook at Meta" button.
channels.instagramWebhookDesc: Meta needs to know where to send the messages. Paste the two values below into the App Dashboard; until then nothing reaches the CRM.
channels.instagramWebhookStep_1: developers.facebook.com → your app → Instagram → API setup with Instagram login → "Configure webhooks".
channels.instagramWebhookStep_2: Paste the Callback URL and the Verify Token and click "Verify and save".
channels.instagramWebhookStep_3: Subscribe to the "messages" field (and "messaging_postbacks", when available).
channels.instagramWebhookStep_4: Make sure the app is published ("Live" mode): in development, only people with a role on the app receive messages.
channels.instagramTokenExpired: Token expired — renew it to receive and reply again.
channels.instagramRenewDesc: Sign in with Instagram again, or generate a new token in the Meta dashboard and paste it here. It must belong to @{username}.
channels.instagramRenewed: Token renewed — valid for another 60 days.
channels.instagramAppDesc: The Instagram App ID and the Instagram App Secret from the Instagram product tab. One app serves every account of the office.
channels.instagramAppIdHint: The number shown in the Instagram product tab, next to the Instagram App Secret — not the app's main ID.
channels.instagramAppSecretKeep: Leave empty to keep the saved secret
channels.instagramAppSecretOptionalHint: Leave empty to use the secret of the saved Meta app — the token must have been generated by that same app.
channels.instagramAppChangeHint: Changing the secret applies to the NEXT connections; the ones already made keep the old secret — reconnect them with Instagram.
channels.instagramAppSaveFailed: Could not save the Meta app.
channels.instagramAppLoadFailed: Could not read the Meta app settings.
channels.instagramRedirectUriHint: Paste it in the Meta dashboard: developers.facebook.com → your app → Instagram → API setup with Instagram login → "Set up Instagram business login" → "Business login settings" → "OAuth redirect URIs". Without it, Instagram refuses the login.
channels.instagramOauthNeedsApp: Save the Meta app above to enable the Instagram login.
channels.instagramManualTitle: Connect with a pasted token instead
channels.instagramOauthError_sessao: Sign in again and retry the Instagram connection.
channels.instagramOauthError_limite: Too many attempts. Wait a minute and try again.
channels.instagramOauthError_sem_app: Save the Meta app before connecting.
channels.instagramOauthError_recusado: The authorization was cancelled in Instagram.
channels.instagramOauthError_estado: The Instagram login did not come back as expected. Start the connection again from this screen.
channels.instagramOauthError_permissao: The account did not grant the messages permission. Connect again keeping the messages permission on.
channels.instagramOauthError_outra_conta: The Instagram {detalhe} is already connected in another account of this CRM.
channels.instagramOauthError_erro: Could not finish the Instagram connection. Try again.
channels.instagramOauthStep_1: Register the OAuth Redirect URI above in the Meta dashboard (once per app).
channels.instagramOauthStep_2: Add the professional account to the app: Instagram → API setup with Instagram login → "Generate access tokens" → add account, and accept the invite in the Instagram app.
channels.instagramOauthSymptom: If Instagram shows an error page instead of the login, the URI above is not registered yet or the account was not added to the app.
channels.instagramWebhookAlreadyToast: The app's webhook is already configured. If you need the values again, use "Webhook at Meta" on the connection.
channels.deleteConfirmInstagramDesc: The connection is removed from the CRM only — nothing changes in the Instagram account or in the Meta app. Conversation history stays in the CRM.
channels.deleteLastChannelInstagram: This is the account's only connection. Deleting it leaves the CRM with no channel. To reconnect, set it up again under "Connect" — nothing changes in the Instagram account.
channels.setDefaultHint: Broadcasts, message templates and the public API always use the default channel.
channels.setDefaultFailed: Could not make this channel the default.
channels.unavailableDesc: The database migration (901) has not been applied to this environment yet. Apply it to manage the workspace's numbers here.
channels.addDescription: Choose how this number talks to the CRM.
channels.chooseMetaDesc: Connects through the Meta Cloud API with an access token. Supports templates and broadcasts.
channels.chooseEvolutionDesc: Pairs a regular WhatsApp by scanning a QR Code. Free-form chat — no templates or broadcasts.
channels.evolutionStepTitle: Connect a number by QR Code
channels.evolutionStepDescription: Creates a new WhatsApp connection on your Evolution server. Just give it a name — you scan the QR Code on the next step.
channels.labelHelpEvolution: Also names the instance on the Evolution server, and that is fixed now — renaming the channel later does not rename the instance.
channels.metaStepDescription: Paste the credentials from the Meta App Dashboard. The CRM verifies them with Meta before saving.
channels.metaVerifyTokenHint: Only needed the first time the Meta app's webhook is set up. Adding another number to an app that already delivers messages? Leave it blank.
channels.metaPinHint: The number's two-step verification PIN (Meta Business Manager → Phone Numbers). Required to register a production number so its inbound messages arrive here. Meta test numbers have no PIN — leave blank.
channels.metaPinInvalid: The PIN must have exactly 6 digits.
channels.metaHelpCreds_1: developers.facebook.com → your app → WhatsApp → API Setup.
channels.metaHelpCreds_2: Copy the number's Phone Number ID and the WhatsApp Business Account ID (WABA).
channels.metaHelpCreds_3: Generate a permanent Access Token in Business Settings → System Users.
channels.metaHelpWebhook_1: If this number belongs to the same Meta app that already delivers messages to this CRM, there is nothing to do — the app's webhook covers all of its numbers.
channels.metaHelpWebhook_2: First number of the app? In WhatsApp → Configuration, set the Callback URL below and a Verify Token of your choice (repeat it in the field above).
channels.metaHelpPin_1: Production numbers must be registered with their two-step PIN so Meta delivers their inbound messages to this CRM.
channels.metaHelpPin_2: Without the PIN the credentials are saved, but the number may stay silent until it is registered.
channels.metaRegistrationSkipped: Credentials verified and saved. Registration was skipped (no PIN) — inbound messages may not arrive until the number is registered.
channels.metaRegistrationFailed: Saved, but Meta could not register the number: {error}
channels.deleteConfirmEvolutionDesc: The CRM removes this connection and asks the Evolution server to drop its instance, unlinking the number from WhatsApp. Conversation history stays in the CRM.
channels.deleteConfirmMetaDesc: The number is removed from the CRM only — nothing changes in your Meta account. Conversation history stays in the CRM.
channels.qrDescription: On your phone: WhatsApp → Settings → Linked devices → Link a device.
channels.qrConnectedDescription: This number is now available as a channel.
channels.qrRefreshHint: The code refreshes every few seconds — that is expected.
channels.connectFailed: Could not reach the Evolution server.
channels.networkError: Network error. Check your connection and try again.
channels.webhookRepairFailed: Could not re-apply the webhook events. Deletions and edits made by the contact may not show up in the CRM.
channels.resyncedToast: Connection resynced. Webhook events were re-applied.
channels.resyncHint: Re-applies the webhook event list on this instance. Use it when deletions or edits made by the contact are not showing up.
channels.fetchPhotosHint: Downloads the WhatsApp profile photo of this connection's contacts (and refreshes the ones older than 30 days)
channels.fetchPhotosStarted: Photo fetch started — they show up in the inbox over the next few minutes
channels.fetchPhotosRunning: A photo fetch is already running for this connection
channels.pipelineNone: None — do not create a deal
channels.pipelineHint: Anyone who writes to this number is added to this pipeline automatically.
channels.pipelineNoStage: Enters pipeline {pipeline}, but no entry stage is set — leads land in whichever stage comes first. Pick one under Configure.
channels.pipelineMissing: The configured pipeline was deleted — pick another one.
channels.pipelineWarning: Applies to contacts without a deal in this pipeline. Every client who writes next becomes a card — and deleting a card by hand does not stop the client from coming back on their next message: to take them out of the pipeline, mark it won or lost.
channels.stageHint: Pick the stage clients should land in. The first column is not always the start of the process.
channels.restartHint: Drops the session and generates a new QR code. Use it when the connection is stuck and Resync did not help.
channels.restartConfirmDesc: The WhatsApp session on this device will drop. The number stops sending and receiving until someone scans the new QR code — have the phone at hand before continuing.
channels.restartKeepsData: Nothing is lost in the CRM: conversations, messages, contacts and this connection settings stay intact.
channels.deleteKeepsHistory: Conversations, messages and contacts from this number are preserved — they simply lose their connection link.
channels.deleteDisablesAutomations: Automations restricted to this number are disabled automatically.
channels.deleteLastChannel: This is the account only connection. Deleting it would leave the CRM without WhatsApp — use "Re-pair" to reconnect the number.
channels.successorHint: The default connection is used for broadcasts, templates and the API. Choose carefully: the office starts sending through it.
channels.restartLocalWarning: You are accessing the CRM from a local address, but this number is the PRODUCTION one. Re-pairing from here takes the real office WhatsApp down.
channels.pipelineUnknown: Pipeline configured — could not load its name.
channels.deleteLastChannelMeta: This is the account only connection. Deleting it would leave the CRM without WhatsApp. To reconnect an official number, set it up again under "Connect a number" — nothing changes in your Meta account.
channels.deleteStopsPipeline: The {pipeline} pipeline stops receiving new clients from this number — the setting is removed along with the connection.
channels.deleteDealsLoseOrigin: Deals created by this number stay in their pipeline but lose their origin record, disappearing from the dashboard breakdown by number.
channels.groupsHint: This number's groups start showing in the inbox alongside chats. No automation, flow or AI reply acts in a group.
channels.groupsResyncWarning: After saving, click Resync on this connection. Without it, messages arrive but join/leave notices don't.
channels.radarHint: AI analyzes this number's conversations (last 7 days): score, urgencies, dissatisfaction and unanswered requests. Off by default.
channels.radarPrivacyWarning: When enabled, this number's conversation content is sent to the account's configured AI provider (your own key). Use the provider's paid tier and confirm the firm's confidentiality policy.

apiKeys.description: Keys authenticate the public REST API (<apiCode>/api/v1</apiCode>) so you can build your own automations. Send them as <headerCode>Authorization: Bearer <key></headerCode>.
apiKeys.createOneHint: Click <bold>New API key</bold> to create one.
apiKeys.askAdminHint: Ask an admin to create one.
apiKeys.scopesHint: A key with no scopes can still call GET /api/v1/me to verify it works.
apiKeys.copyDesc: This is the only time the full key is shown. Store it somewhere safe — if you lose it, revoke it and create a new one.
apiKeys.copyFailed: Copy failed — select and copy manually
apiKeys.newKeyDesc: Name it after the integration that will use it, and grant only the scopes it needs.

aiConfig.title: Agent setup
aiConfig.description: Bring your own OpenAI, Anthropic or Google (Gemini) key. This CRM calls the provider directly with your key — no per-seat AI fees, and your data stays yours. This powers AI-drafted replies in the inbox, the auto-reply bot, the Playground and the Service Radar.
aiConfig.adminOnlyConfig: Only admins and owners can change the AI configuration.
aiConfig.encryptionNotice: Your key is encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM) and never shown again after saving.

legenda.intro: The Radar flags; the operator always decides. Here is what it reads, what it computes and when it runs.
legenda.escopo: Only channels with the Radar enabled (Settings → Connections) and only 1:1 conversations — groups stay out. The AI receives only the messages from the last {dias} days: a conversation's older history is never sent, even when it is months old. Deleted messages stay out; audio and media without text are not read — the card states how many were left out of the analysis. A client waiting for a reply never expires: the idle conversation stays on the panel while the pending reply is open.
legenda.limites: In a very long conversation, the {mensagens} most recent messages of the window go in — when that happens, the expanded card says the oldest ones were left out. Automated menus and notices the bot repeats go in only once.
legenda.nota: The score (0–10) starts at 10 and deducts for unjustified delays, ignored or half-answered requests, curt tone and lack of proactivity. Response times are not estimated by the AI: the system computes them in business hours (Mon–Fri, {abre}h–{fecha}h, São Paulo time) — nights and weekends do not count as delay.
legenda.alarme: The panel lists only conversations with a problem: dissatisfaction, an unanswered client request, legal urgency (summons, subpoena, bailiff, asset freeze, deadline, hearing) or a client waiting more than {horas}h. A well-handled conversation is still analysed and still counts towards the average score above, but it never becomes a card for someone to handle. Case mentions and points of attention show up inside an open card — on their own, they do not open one. The wait only ends when a PERSON replies: automated messages (broadcast, automation, scheduled) do not clear it. As soon as someone replies, the card leaves the list immediately, without waiting for the next analysis.
legenda.sinais: Urgency, dissatisfaction, unanswered requests, lawsuit mentions and attention points are identified by the AI — and every signal requires evidence: the actual message excerpt that justifies it is shown on the card. A signal without evidence is discarded automatically before reaching the screen. Case numbers (CNJ pattern) are also detected by a fixed rule, without AI. For team managers, the analysis includes per-agent observations (delays, confusing messages, unanswered questions), citing that person's own messages.
legenda.ciclo: Automatic cycle every ~{ciclo} min, in small batches, starting with the most recently active conversations. The same conversation waits at least {espera} min between analyses and only re-enters the queue when there is a new message — an idle conversation costs nothing (a failed analysis retries up to 3 times). A window with no client messages (broadcast, outreach) does not trigger the AI: metrics only, and automated messages do not close a pending reply — only a human one does. "Reanalyze" forces an analysis right away.
legenda.estados: "Handled" moves the card out of the way and reopens by itself if the client sends a message afterwards — also use it to archive a conversation that ended with a client courtesy ("ok, thanks") and got flagged as waiting. "Dismissed" means "the AI got this one wrong": it never reopens on its own and is recorded as a false positive for calibration. Both buttons offer "Undo" right after the click, and the card STAYS on the list — dimmed, with a "Reopen" button — while this screen is open: a mistaken click can be fixed either way. Leaving the screen clears the list, like the end of a triage shift.
legenda.custo: The Radar's AI usage shows up under Settings → AI Agents, as the "radar" mode.
